title: Regulate taxis and ride-share for safety, not to limit numbers
action: Remove any remaining caps on taxi licences and rules that protect taxis from ride-share and hire cars, and regulate all point-to-point services through an independent body for minimum safety and consumer standards.
why: Licence caps raised fares and created valuable plates instead of better service; where caps were lifted and ride-share allowed, supply and innovation rose.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Taxis and ride-sharing: in particular, regulations that restrict numbers of taxi licences and competition in the taxi industry, including from ride-sharing and other passenger transport services that compete with taxis.

evidence.source: Competition Policy Review: Final Report (Harper review)
evidence.quote: Regulation of taxi and hire car services should be focused on ensuring minimum standards for the benefit of consumers rather than on restricting competition or supporting a particular business model. An independent body should oversee the regulations.

progress.what: Every jurisdiction has legalised ride-share; South Australia removed its metropolitan taxi licence cap in 2025.
